money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Poland's currency is the Zloty (PLN). You can easily change all major currencies. If you're travelling between Poland and any non-EU country, declare currency equivalent to 10,000 euro or more. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. You'll be fined if you don't declare currency or give incorrect information. You should check with local authorities in the countries you are leaving, entering or passing through whether you must declare higher amounts of currency.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They include mandatory prison sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: There are strict alcohol laws. If you drink and drive, you face up to five years in jail and substantial fines. The blood alcohol limit is 0.02%. Your car could also be impounded. Drink drivers involved in accidents face up to 16 years in jail and significant fines. It's illegal to be drunk in public, including parks and picnic areas. You may be arrested or taken to a facility to sober up. Expect to pay for the cost of your stay.
laws.heading: Drinking laws

laws.rule: Poland has no specific surrogacy laws in place. Seek independent legal advice. The Australian Embassy can't provide: legal advice about surrogacy information on clinics
laws.heading: Surrogacy

laws.rule: It's illegal to take photos of some buildings. Look for signs on buildings that forbid photos. If you're not sure, check with local authorities.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: You can drive for up to 6 months. You must carry both your Australian driver's licence (digital driver’s licences may not be accepted) and an International Driving Permit (IDP). Get your IDP before you leave Australia. Driving using only your Australian driver’s licence without the IDP is considered a serious offence. visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Poland is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Officials may ask for an onward ticket; land borders from Belarus and Russia are closed to entry.
